products.name: Atlantic Salmon Portions (farmed)
products.score_rationale: Every food here starts with 60 points. −8 — farm-raised fish. −4 — its pink color comes from pigment added to the feed (wild salmon is pink on its own). −4 — its fats run about 14 times more out of balance than wild salmon. +5 — the farm is certified to better rules than most. Add it up: 49. Wild sockeye earns points for exactly the things this fish loses them on.
products.description: Farm-raised Atlantic salmon. FARMED VS WILD, THE CURRENT TRUTH: farmed salmon's pink is synthetic astaxanthin added to the feed — U.S. law requires 'color added' on the label. Its omega-6-to-omega-3 ratio runs about 14 times worse than wild (0.7 vs 0.05). And antibiotic use depends on where it's farmed: Chile has used ~500 times more antibiotics per tonne than Norway. The old '10x more PCBs' claim is outdated — feed changed, and current European data shows wild Atlantic salmon now carries MORE dioxins and mercury than farmed. We tell it as the data reads today. BAP certification and Norwegian-style practice are the better end of farming — but wild sockeye needs no color additive and carries the ancestral omega ratio on its own. THE INGREDIENTS: Atlantic salmon (color added through feed). THE FLAGS: 'Color added through feed' — farmed salmon flesh is naturally gray, and pigment in the feed turns it pink. Federal law makes the label admit it. One ingredient on paper; the parenthesis is the tell.

Mercury is a non-issue for shrimp (FDA mean 0.009 ppm), but imported farmed shrimp is where FDA import screens most often find banned-antibiotic residues, and the bag rarely says which country's farm it came from. products.description: USDA Organic ground beef at a store-brand price — organic means certified feed, no antibiotics, no added hormones, audited yearly. The label doesn't claim 100% grass-fed, so it doesn't score the grass bonus. LABEL DECODER: 'No added hormones' on chicken or pork is pure marketing — federal law bans hormones in ALL U.S. poultry and pork, and the label is legally required to admit it. On beef, hormone implants ARE legal and common in feedlots. And 'grass-fed' lost its federal definition in 2016 — without third-party certification, it's a self-declared claim. THE INGREDIENTS: Sold under the federal 'ground beef' standard — which by law bars added water, binders and extenders — and USDA Organic. Trader Joe's doesn't publish the full panel online, and we don't guess at labels. THE FLAGS: None expected on a single-ingredient organic grind — check the pack to confirm.

products.name: Organic Oven Roasted Chicken Breast (sliced)
products.score_rationale: Every food here starts with 60 points. +12 — certified organic. +5 — outside inspectors check it. +4 — no antibiotics ever. Then −12 — sliced deli meat is processed meat, full stop. Add it up: 69. Good sourcing can't undo the deli part.
products.description: The cleanest version of deli chicken: USDA Organic, no antibiotics ever, humanely raised, no chemical nitrates. Still deli meat — processed meat carries a score penalty no sourcing can erase. LABEL DECODER: 'No added hormones' on chicken or pork is pure marketing — federal law bans hormones in ALL U.S. poultry and pork, and the label is legally required to admit it. On beef, hormone implants ARE legal and common in feedlots. And 'grass-fed' lost its federal definition in 2016 — without third-party certification, it's a self-declared claim. THE INGREDIENTS: Organic chicken breast, organic chicken broth, then 2% or less: sea salt, organic potato starch, rosemary extract. THE FLAGS: Organic chicken broth — added liquid pumped into the meat, so part of what you're paying for is water. Organic potato starch — the binder that holds that added moisture in the slice. Rosemary extract — a natural antioxidant that keeps the fat from going rancid; the mildest of the three. No celery powder and no carrageenan, which puts this ahead of most deli meat.

LABEL DECODER: 'No added hormones' on chicken or pork is pure marketing — federal law bans hormones in ALL U.S. poultry and pork, and the label is legally required to admit it. products.description: The rare hot dog with receipts: USDA Organic, 100% grass-fed AND certified regeneratively sourced beef, no antibiotics ever, humanely raised. Still a processed meat — penalty applied — but the sourcing stack is stronger than most raw meat on the shelf. LABEL DECODER: 'No added hormones' on chicken or pork is marketing — hormones are federally banned in ALL U.S. poultry and pork; the label must admit it. 'Grass-fed' lost its federal definition in 2016; certification is the real signal. THE INGREDIENTS: Organic grass-fed beef and water, then under 2%: sea salt, organic vinegar, baking soda, organic garlic, organic paprika, organic spices (black pepper, coriander, ginger, mace, cayenne), organic dehydrated onion, cultured celery powder. Celery powder is concentrated natural nitrate, and it cures this hot dog exactly the way sodium nitrite cures a conventional one. 'Uncured' on the front of the pack is a labeling loophole, not a nitrate-free promise. Everything else on this label is clean.
